name: library
title: Open-source library
summary: Your users get a changelog line and the right version bump, every release.

rules.text: A breaking change bumps the major version.
rules.why: people pin a major version, so a breaking change must never arrive inside one; before 1.0 people pin the minor version, so there a breaking change bumps the minor.

rules.text: Every public function has a working example in the docs.
rules.why: an example that runs teaches a function fastest and breaks loudly when the function changes.

rules.text: Every release adds a changelog line for each change its users can see.
rules.why: the changelog is where users learn what an upgrade changes, so a change left out of it surprises them.

items.title: Every docs example runs as a test
items.criterion: Every example in the docs runs as part of the test suite, so a change that breaks an example fails the tests. test/docs-examples.test.js runs each example and fails before the change.
items.brief:
Files:
- test/docs-examples.test.js
Test:
- test/docs-examples.test.js reads each example from the docs, runs it, and fails when one throws

items.title: Removing a public name fails until the major version goes up
items.criterion: A recorded list of the library's public names is compared with what it exports, and a removed or renamed name fails the tests unless the major version went up. test/public-api.test.js holds that comparison and fails before the change.
items.brief:
Files:
- test/public-api.json (the recorded public names)
- test/public-api.test.js
Test:
- test/public-api.test.js compares the exports with the recorded names and the version in package.json
